liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Casey Jones** (1 review): Opener was halted about a minute in, then restarted from the beginning after the band shared a joint [12]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 other source): Will Scott played harmonica on a starred song; Chinacat Sunflower and Uncle John's Band are missing from the tape [1]
- **Not Fadeaway** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the Not Fade Away as a standout, aided by the soundboard [2]
- Reviewer recalls an Uncle John's Band opening with only bass and harmonica for about eight bars, absent from this copy [4]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-11-23.sbd.lai.4734.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 13 songs; 74 min; rated 2.55/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: Surviving soundboard portions sound very good despite cuts and missing tracks; Weir's vocals and rhythm playing stand out; Recording is good quality with strong jams, though tracks lack labels for streaming [3][10]

## Around the show

- Show was played for a worthy cause and featured some very special guests [3]
- Show was a benefit with a two-dollar admission, which the reviewer found questionable regarding Hell's Angels [11]
- Venue was across from the Fillmore; band stopped a minute into Casey Jones to pass a joint, then restarted [12]
- Winwood, Capaldi, Wood and Ramblin' Jack Elliot joined the band on one song [1]
- Says this is largely an excerpt of the 11/16 Fillmore show, with the same Not Fade Away jam featuring Winwood [5]
- Claims missing parts can be found on 11/16/1970, suggesting this recording may be mislabeled [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-11-23.sbd.lai.4734.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Mike Lai; source: SBDMR>DAT>CD-r>EAC>SHN [1]. Also: Reviewer owns a soundboard cassette of the show that includes an Uncle John's Band encore, transferred to FLAC [7]
